subject: QSO
question: Qanoon-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 is _____.
explanation: Evidence law governs how facts are proved in proceedings; it is generally classified as procedural law.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: There are _____ articles in the Qanoon-e-Shahadat Order 1984.
explanation: The numbered sequence ends at Article 166. Later inserted articles such as 46-A do not change that conventional exam answer.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: The Qanoon-e-Shahadat Order 1984 extends to the whole of Pakistan and applies to all judicial proceedings before any forum, EXCEPT _____.
options: Authority exercising judicial or quasi-judicial proceedings
explanation: Article 1 expressly excludes proceedings before an arbitrator. Courts martial and tribunals are included.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under the Qanoon-e-Shahadat Order, 1984, “That a man holds a certain opinion, has a certain intention, acts in good faith or fraudulently, or uses a particular word in a particular sense or is or was at a specified time conscious of a particular sensation” is a _____.
explanation: A conscious mental condition is a fact. The book key says B, but the statutory illustration explicitly says fact: D.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A fact in issue is a fact _____.
options: Asserted by one and denied by other party
explanation: B is the closest short description. More precisely, facts in issue determine the existence, extent or nature of an asserted or denied right, liability or disability.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: One fact is said to be _____ to another when the one is connected with the other in any of the ways referred to in the provisions of the Order relating to the relevancy of facts.
explanation: Relevance is the connection recognised by the Order. Dispute and corroboration are different concepts.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: As per the Qanoon-e-Shahadat, 1984, Court includes all judges and magistrates and all persons, except _____, legally authorized to take evidence.
explanation: The definition excludes arbitrators even though other people legally authorised to take evidence can be included.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Mr. A sues Mr. B for trespass on his land. Mr. B alleges a public right of way, which Mr. A denies. A decree in favour of C in an earlier suit by A against C for trespass on the same land, in which C alleged the same right of way, _____.
options: Is a conclusive evidence in favour of Mr. C
Is relevant, but it is not conclusive proof
Is relevant and it is a conclusive proof for the right of way exists
explanation: A judgment about a matter of public nature is relevant but not conclusive. The book key incorrectly selects C; the illustration supports B.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: As per Article 2(b) of the Qanoon-e-Shahadat Order 1984, _____ means any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks, or by more than one of those means, intended to be used, or which may be used, for recording that matter.
explanation: The defined term is document. A map, inscription or caricature can qualify, not only a signed legal instrument.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: As per Article 2(1)(c)(i), _____ refers to “all statements which the Court permits or requires be made before it by witnesses, in relation to matters of fact under inquiry”.
explanation: Witness statements permitted or required before court are oral evidence; documents produced for inspection are documentary evidence.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: According to Article 2(1)(d), _____ includes anything, state of things, or relation of things capable of being perceived by the senses and any mental condition of which any person is conscious.
explanation: Facts include sensory matters and conscious mental conditions, so the concept is wider than physical objects alone.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: As per Article 2(2), one fact is said to be relevant to another when connected with it in any of the ways referred to in the provisions of the Order relating to _____.
explanation: The wording is relevancy of facts. Everyday importance does not replace statutory relevance.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: As per Article 2(6), a fact is said not to be proved when it is _____.
explanation: Not proved is the middle category: the court has neither accepted existence nor accepted non-existence.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: When one fact is declared conclusive proof of another, the Court shall regard the other as proved and _____ allow evidence for the purpose of disproving it.
explanation: Conclusive proof stops rebuttal of that consequence. Shall presume, by contrast, remains rebuttable.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 3, a person convicted for perjury or giving false evidence is not a competent witness unless the court is satisfied that he _____.
options: Got a certificate from the court to testify
Has repented and has mended his ways
explanation: The express exception requires the court to be satisfied about repentance and reform, not a certificate or one outward practice.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 3, a lunatic is competent to testify if not prevented by his lunacy from understanding the _____.
options: Case scenario and giving rational statement
Nature of crime and giving response to them
Substance of the case and giving explanation
Questions put to him and giving rational answers to them
explanation: Competence depends on understanding questions and giving rational answers. The diagnosis alone does not disqualify.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A person is not competent to testify if he has been convicted by the court for _____.
explanation: Both convictions engage the exclusion, subject to the express repentance-and-reform exception.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: No Judge or Magistrate shall, except on special order of a superior Court, be compelled to answer as to his judicial conduct or knowledge; but as to other matters occurring in his presence whilst acting, _____.
explanation: The protection concerns judicial conduct or knowledge as judge. Other events witnessed in court can be examined.
cue: Judicial conduct protected; other events examinable
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A is accused before the Court of Session of attempting to murder a police officer whilst on trial before B, a Sessions Judge. B _____ be examined as to what occurred.
explanation: B witnessed a separate occurrence, not merely a matter of judicial conduct. The illustration says he may be examined.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 6, no one shall give evidence derived from _____ official records relating to affairs of State except with permission of the head of department.
explanation: The provision uses unpublished official records. Permission rests with the head of the department concerned.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: “Official records relating to the affairs of State” _____ documents concerning industrial or commercial activities carried on by Government or a body or company set up or controlled by it.
explanation: The explanation expressly includes government industrial and commercial documents.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A tells advocate B: “I wish to obtain possession of property by use of a forged deed on which I request you to sue.” This communication, made in furtherance of a criminal purpose, is _____.
explanation: Privilege does not protect communication furthering an illegal purpose. Asking for defence about a past offence is a different situation.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Mr. Dewood asks attorney Mr. Behram to sue using a forged document to obtain property. Under Article 9, this is _____.
options: Dependent upon the nature of charge
explanation: The client is requesting help to carry out fraud, bringing the communication within the illegal-purpose exception.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: No one shall be compelled to produce documents which another person could refuse to produce, unless that other person _____.
explanation: Possession by a third person does not defeat the underlying privilege. The entitled person's consent is the stated exception.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 15, a witness _____ be excused from answering a relevant question on the ground that the answer will criminate him.
explanation: Shall not is the statutory wording. Compelled answers receive protection from arrest/prosecution or use against the witness, except prosecution for false evidence.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: An accomplice is competent against an accused except in the case of an offence punishable with _____.
explanation: Hadd is the express exception. The article also says an uncorroborated accomplice conviction is not illegal merely for that reason; prudential corroboration remains important.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: In financial or future obligations reduced to writing, the instrument shall be attested by _____.
options: Two men or one man and two women
explanation: This is the specific written financial/future obligation rule, subject to special law. Do not apply it to every kind of case.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Unless Hudood or special law provides otherwise, in all other matters the Court may act on testimony of _____ or other evidence warranted by circumstances.
explanation: The general residual provision permits one man or one woman. It differs from the specific attestation rule for written obligations.
cue: Other matters: one man or woman
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 18, _____ may be given of existence or non-existence of facts in issue and other facts declared relevant.
explanation: Evidence concerns facts in issue and legally relevant facts; it is not limited to documents.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Which Article provides that evidence can be given regarding facts in issue and relevant facts?
explanation: Article 18 is the gateway relevance rule. Article 30 defines admission.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Relevant facts are those facts which _____.
options: Are relevant in accordance with any law other than Qanun-e-Shahadat Order
Are declared to be relevant by the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order
Appear to be relevant from the circumstances
explanation: The book selects D, but apparent everyday relevance alone is not enough. The options do not clearly distinguish statutory relevance from factual relevance. Keep out of scored mocks.
cue: Legal relevance needs a recognised connection
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Mr. A sues Mr. B for Rs. 1,000 and shows entries in his account books showing B indebted. The entries are _____ without other evidence to prove the debt.
options: Except the contents of classified documents
explanation: Regular business account entries are relevant but cannot alone charge a person with liability.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: The doctrine of “Res gestae” is incorporated in Article _____ of Qanoon-e-Shahadat Order.
explanation: Article 19 concerns facts forming part of the same transaction.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 19, facts connected with a _____ so as to form part of the same transaction are relevant.
explanation: The connection must be with a fact in issue as part of the same transaction, whether at the same or different times and places.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A is accused of murdering B by beating him. Whatever was said or done by A, B or the _____ at or shortly before or after the beating, forming part of the transaction, is relevant.
explanation: The illustration includes bystanders' contemporaneous statements or acts forming part of the transaction.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Article 20 is an exception to which rule of evidence?
options: Evidence of facts similar to but not part of the main fact is not generally admissible to prove its existence
Exclusion of character when character is not in issue
explanation: The book selects A. Article 20 itself addresses occasion, cause, effect and opportunity; the broad “exception” formulation is imprecise. Do not memorise it as the wording of the article.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A is tried for murdering B by poison. Before B's death A procured poison similar to that administered. This fact is _____.
explanation: Procuring poison is preparation. Relevant is the statutory answer; important and pertinent are everyday synonyms.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Article 22 deals with _____.
options: Relevancy of facts forming part of some transactions
Motive, preparation and previous or subsequent conduct
Facts necessary to explain or introduce relevant facts
Things said or done by conspirator in reference to common design
explanation: Explanation and introduction belong to Article 22; transaction is 19, motive is 21, conspiracy is 23.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A sues B for inducing C to break a service contract with A. On leaving, C says “I am leaving you because B has made me a better offer.” This statement is _____ as explanatory of C's conduct.
explanation: The statement explains the relevant conduct. The book has a service-party typo; the statutory illustration concerns C leaving A's service.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Which Article contains the plea of alibi?
explanation: Presence elsewhere can make the alleged presence highly improbable or impossible; Article 24 addresses inconsistent facts.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 24(1), otherwise irrelevant facts become relevant if _____ with a fact in issue or relevant fact.
explanation: Inconsistency is the first limb. The second includes facts making existence or non-existence highly probable or improbable.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A is accused of receiving stolen goods knowing them stolen. Possession at the same time of many other stolen articles is _____ as tending to show knowledge.
explanation: Other stolen articles can show the particular guilty knowledge, rather than merely bad character.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Article 28 concerns whether an act was _____ or done with particular knowledge or intention.
explanation: A series of similar occurrences can help distinguish accident from intention. This is the statutory topic.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Statements by parties suing or sued in a representative character are _____ unless made while holding that character.
explanation: The timing and representative capacity matter. A personal statement outside that capacity does not automatically bind the represented interest.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A undertakes to collect B's rents. B sues A for failing to collect rent due from C. A denies that rent was due. C's statement that he owed B rent is _____.
explanation: C's liability must be established against A; the specified statement can be relevant as an admission.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: The question is whether a horse sold by A to B is sound. A says “Go and ask C, C knows all about it.” C's statement is _____.
explanation: A expressly referred B to C for information, so C's statement is an admission in this context.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 34, _____ are relevant and may be proved against the person making them or his representative in interest, but generally not by or on behalf of the maker.
explanation: The article says admissions and lists exceptions allowing a maker to prove them. A party cannot generally manufacture evidence for himself through his own admission.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Oral admissions about contents of a document are _____ unless the party shows entitlement to secondary evidence of its contents.
explanation: Not relevant is the general rule. Another statutory exception is where genuineness of a produced document is in question.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Tahir and Harris are jointly tried for murdering Khawar. Harris said “I and Tahir murdered Khawar for money.” The confession is proof against _____ and may be circumstantial evidence against _____.
explanation: It is proof against the maker Harris and may be considered circumstantial evidence against jointly tried Tahir. Joint trial for the same offence is essential.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 36, in _____ no admission is relevant if made on an express condition that evidence of it is not to be given, or circumstances show that agreement.
explanation: The rule applies in civil cases to admissions made under the specified non-use condition.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 38, no confession made to a _____ shall be proved against a person accused of an offence.
explanation: The officer category is police officer. Separately, Article 40 allows the part of information distinctly related to a discovered fact.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Confession before a police officer _____.
options: Cannot be proved against the person making it
explanation: The general bar is Article 38. Do not confuse it with the narrowly provable discovery information under Article 40.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Which of the following is not a true statement?
options: All confessions are admissions but not vice versa
All confessions made under undue influence can be proved against the maker
Admitted facts by the adverse party need not be proved
explanation: C is false because the specified inducement, threat or promise excludes a confession. The book key selects B, but B expresses the usual admission/confession distinction. Article 113 preserves the court's power to require proof.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: The question whether a confession is voluntary or not _____.
options: Is a pure question of fact
Is a mixed question of law and fact
Is a pure question of law
Depends upon discretion of the court
explanation: The book selects A. Whether particular pressure occurred is factual, while the legal test for admissibility is a legal question. Without a cited controlling judgment this broad classification is kept out of scored mocks.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A confession under Article 37 made after the impression of inducement, threat or promise has been fully removed in the Court's opinion is _____.
explanation: Removal must be complete in the court's opinion. The earlier pressure does not forever exclude every later confession.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 42, an otherwise relevant confession does not become irrelevant only because _____.
options: It is made in police station
It is not made with free consent of the confessor
It was made when the confessor was drunk
explanation: Drunkenness alone is listed as insufficient to exclude an otherwise relevant confession. The article expressly does not apply to Hudood trials; police bars and coercion rules still matter.
cue: Otherwise relevant; drunkenness alone no bar
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Where persons are jointly tried for the same offence, a proved confession is proof against its maker and may be considered _____ evidence against the other person.
explanation: The precise term is circumstantial. It does not become the same direct proof against every co-accused.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Admissions are not conclusive proof but may operate as _____.
explanation: An admission may stop a person denying a representation when the requirements for estoppel are met; it is not automatically conclusive proof.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: There are _____ parties in estoppel.
explanation: The basic relationship is between the person who induces belief and the person who relies on it, including their representatives.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Article 46, among other things, deals with _____.
explanation: Cause-of-death statements fall within Article 46. It also covers several other categories of unavailable-person statements.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A dying declaration relates to the cause of the maker's death, _____ the maker was under expectation of death.
explanation: Pakistan's statutory rule does not require expectation of death when the statement was made.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Article 46 applies when a person's statement concerns the _____ or circumstances of the transaction resulting in his death, where its cause comes into question.
explanation: The rule is about the cause of that person's death and the fatal transaction, not only murder cases.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A sues B for libel in a painted caricature displayed in a shop window. The remarks of a crowd about its similarity and libellous character _____ cannot be proved.
explanation: The book stem accidentally appends “cannot be proved” after the blank. The statutory illustration says the remarks may be proved, and the key is B. Malformed stem excluded from scored mocks.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Dying declaration of a child is _____.
explanation: Childhood alone does not impose a blanket bar. Capacity and reliability must still be assessed; admissible does not mean automatically true.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: _____ is the exception to the general rule that oral evidence shall be direct.
explanation: A qualifying dying declaration can be proved although its maker is unavailable for direct testimony. Other admissibility doctrines also exist; this is the intended option.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Entries in regularly kept business books are relevant, but alone insufficient to charge any person with _____.
explanation: Liability is the statutory word. Account entries require supporting evidence against the person charged.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Existence of a judgment, order or decree preventing a Court from taking cognizance or holding a trial is a _____ when that bar is in question.
explanation: A previous judgment is relevant to decide whether a later suit or trial is legally barred.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 56, judgments other than those in Article 55 are relevant if they relate to matters of a public _____ relevant to the inquiry.
explanation: The precise word is nature. Such judgments are relevant but not conclusive proof of their statements.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: “Expert” means _____.
options: A person who is more skillful
A person who is well qualified and holds recognition of law
A person skilled by special study or experience with adequate knowledge of the subject
explanation: Special skill in the relevant field supports expert opinion. General cleverness or a title alone is not the test.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Whether A was poisoned is in question. Other people poisoned by that poison showed symptoms which experts affirm or deny to be its symptoms. This is _____.
options: Dependent upon permission of the Court
explanation: Facts supporting or contradicting a relevant expert opinion are relevant too.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 61, when the court has _____ as to who wrote or signed a document, the opinion of someone acquainted with that handwriting is relevant.
explanation: Acquaintance with handwriting can make an opinion relevant. This is distinct from only using a handwriting expert.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Divorce pronounced during death illness is _____.
explanation: The book marks C. This is a Muslim personal-law issue rather than an evidence-rule question; effect and inheritance consequences need separate authority and facts. Excluded pending verification.
reference: No QSO provision supports the keyed rule
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: In civil cases, character offered to render _____ the conduct imputed is irrelevant, except where character appears from otherwise relevant facts.
explanation: The exact pair is probable or improbable. Character can still matter when independently relevant, including damages under Article 69.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: In criminal proceedings the accused's good character is _____.
explanation: Previous good character of an accused is expressly relevant; the rule for bad character is different.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 68 _____.
options: Evidence of bad character except in reply is inadmissible
Evidence of bad character is admissible in all cases
Evidence of bad character is admissible only in capital trials
explanation: Bad character is generally irrelevant unless answering evidence of good character. The article also addresses character itself being in issue and previous convictions.
cue: Bad character: generally no; reply exception
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: In criminal proceedings the fact that the accused has a bad character is _____.
options: Dependent upon the nature of charge
explanation: A states the general rule, subject to the good-character reply exception and the article's explanations.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: “All facts, _____, may be proved by oral evidence.”
options: Except the contents of classified documents
Except the contents of unattested documents
explanation: The exception is contents of documents generally, not merely classified or unattested documents.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: The contents of documents may be proved _____.
options: Either by primary or by secondary evidence
explanation: Primary or secondary evidence may prove contents, but secondary evidence must meet its statutory conditions.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: “Primary evidence” means the document itself produced for the _____ of the Court.
explanation: Inspection is the statutory wording. The original document is the core example, with explanatory rules for counterparts and copies.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Certified copies, qualifying mechanical copies, compared copies, counterparts against non-executing parties, and oral accounts by someone who saw the document are included in _____.
explanation: These are categories of secondary evidence. Falling in a category does not dispense with the conditions for using it.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Article 76 deals with cases where _____ evidence may be given.
explanation: Article 76 lists situations permitting secondary evidence of documents.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 76(b), when the original's existence, condition or contents are admitted in writing by the opposite party or representative, the _____ admission is admissible.
explanation: The written admission is the allowed proof in that case. An oral admission is not what this clause specifies.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: If an attesting witness denies or cannot recollect execution of a document, execution may be proved by _____ evidence.
explanation: Other evidence is the article's wording; the witness's denial or lost memory does not make proof impossible.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Which of the following is not a public document?
options: Judgment of Supreme Court of Pakistan in CRP No. 296/2020
Official gazette of Pakistan for year 2020
Unregistered MOU between Faisal Steel Pvt Ltd and All Construction Pvt Ltd
explanation: The book selects D, a private MOU. But a company prospectus is not necessarily a public document merely because circulated publicly; public records of private documents differ. Ambiguous without more facts, so excluded.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Government maps are presumed accurate, but maps made for purposes of any cause _____ proved to be accurate.
explanation: Litigation-specific maps need proof; the ordinary government-map presumption does not automatically settle their accuracy.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A enters a written contract with B to work B's mines. A was induced by a/an _____ of B as to their value. This fact may be proved.
explanation: Misrepresentation can be proved despite the written contract. The rule excluding oral variation does not protect invalidating facts.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Evidence may not be presented of _____.
explanation: Book key B intends “admitted facts need not be proved,” not “may not.” The Court can still require proof. The stem converts an exemption into a prohibition, so exclude from scored mocks.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A falsely induces B to buy land by saying it belongs to A. A later acquires it and tries to set aside the sale because he lacked title originally. He _____ be allowed to prove that lack of title.
explanation: Estoppel prevents A denying the representation on which B acted. The key expects mandatory “must not”; B is linguistically close.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A wants the Court to punish B for a crime A says B committed. A _____ that B committed the crime.
options: May allege the same before a Judge
Shall take oath to that effect
explanation: The person seeking judgment on asserted facts must prove them. Allegation alone is not proof.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: In a criminal case, if the prosecution fails to discharge its burden _____.
options: Burden shifts to the accused to prove innocence
The prosecution is given a chance to reinvestigate
explanation: Failure to prove the charge leads to acquittal, subject to applicable statutory rules. It does not generally make the accused prove innocence.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 118, burden of proof lies on _____ who would fail if no evidence were given on either side.
explanation: The no-evidence test identifies the burden bearer; it is not invariably one named procedural role.
cue: Ask: who loses with no evidence?
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A sues B for land B possesses, asserting that C, B's father, left it to A by will. Burden of proof lies on _____.
explanation: Without evidence B keeps possession, so claimant A must prove the will and entitlement: option C. The book key marks option A (person B), which contradicts Article 118's illustration.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: If a person has not been heard of for _____ years by those who naturally would hear of him, the burden of proving him alive shifts to whoever affirms it.
explanation: Seven years shifts the burden about being alive. It does not by itself prove the exact date of death.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 126, where a person is shown in _____, the burden of proving he is not owner lies on whoever asserts that.
explanation: Shown possession supports the ownership presumption, placing the stated burden on the challenger.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 128, birth during valid marriage and not earlier than _____ lunar months from marriage, or within two years after dissolution with mother unmarried, is conclusive proof subject to the article's exceptions.
explanation: The minimum stated is six lunar months. Read it with the statutory exceptions rather than treating every birth date as automatically conclusive.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Examination in chief is _____.
options: The examination in court of law
The examination of a witness by the party who called him
The examination of a witness by the opposite party
explanation: The calling party conducts chief; the adverse party conducts cross.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Subsequent examination by the calling party after cross-examination by the adverse party is _____.
explanation: Re-examination follows cross and ordinarily explains matters raised in cross.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: The accomplice is unworthy of credit, thus _____.
explanation: Article 129 permits the prudential presumption requiring material corroboration. Article 16 still says an uncorroborated conviction is not illegal merely for that reason, outside Hadd.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: If new matter is introduced in re-examination with the Court's permission, the adverse party may further _____ on that matter.
explanation: Fresh matter permits further cross-examination about that matter, maintaining the adverse party's opportunity to test it.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 138, leading questions may be asked in _____.
explanation: Cross is the express general permission. Leading in chief/re needs the separate Article 137 exceptions or permission.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 141(3), in cross-examination a witness _____ be asked questions tending to shake credit by injuring character, although answers may criminate him or expose him to penalty.
explanation: May is the statutory permission, controlled by later protections against groundless, indecent or insulting questions.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: The Court may forbid _____ questions or inquiries, though bearing on the case, unless relating to facts in issue or necessary to decide them.
explanation: Indecent/scandalous questions may be forbidden unless within the stated necessity exception. Distinguish Article 148's insulting/annoying questions.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 148, the Court shall forbid questions intended to _____ or needlessly offensive in form.
explanation: Shall forbid is mandatory for these abusive questions.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A witness denies dismissal from employment for dishonesty. Evidence offered merely to contradict him about that dismissal is _____.
explanation: A collateral answer testing credit generally cannot be contradicted with other evidence. The article has specific exceptions such as a denied previous conviction.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 150, the Court may permit the party calling a witness to ask questions that could be put in cross-examination by the _____.
explanation: Court permission allows cross-style questioning of one's own witness. It is not an automatic entitlement.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Article 151 deals with _____.
options: Procedure of Court in cases of defamation, libel and slander
Exclusion of evidence to contradict answers testing veracity
Question by party to his own witness
explanation: Impeachment of credit belongs to 151; own-witness questions to 150; collateral contradiction to 149.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: The credit of a witness may be impeached by the _____.
options: Adverse party with the permission of the court
Both parties without permission of the court
Adverse party and with the permission of the court the party who calls him
explanation: The adverse party may impeach; the calling party needs the Court's consent.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: A party who refuses to produce a document after notice _____ afterwards use it in evidence without the other party's consent or Court's order.
explanation: Cannot is the article's wording. Consent or a court order supplies the exception.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Leading questions may be asked in _____.
explanation: The book key B states the general rule. But chief can also permit leading questions under Article 137. Without a general-rule qualification, C is defensible; keep this duplicate out of scored mocks.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: When plaintiff takes oath in support of his claim, the Court _____, on plaintiff's application, call on defendant to deny the claim on oath.
explanation: Shall is mandatory on the described application. The mechanism does not apply to Hudood enforcement laws or other criminal cases.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 163(1), the Court calls upon the defendant _____ the claim on oath.
explanation: The statutory step is denial on oath; it is not a general oath-based shortcut for criminal convictions.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 164, where modern devices make evidence available _____.
options: It is binding on the Court to consider such evidence
It is binding on the Court not to consider such evidence
It is in the discretion of the Court to consider such evidence
explanation: The court may allow appropriate modern-device evidence. It is not automatic acceptance of authenticity or truth.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: In cases the Court considers appropriate, it _____ allow evidence available because of modern devices or techniques.
explanation: The word is may. Reliability and other admissibility requirements still matter.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: QSO
question: Under Article 164, CCTV footage of an incident that is a fact in issue is _____ in evidence before court.
explanation: CCTV can be admitted under Article 164 subject to court assessment and proper proof. The question's “admissible” means capable of admission, not automatically authentic.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: The Pakistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Council Rules were formulated in the year _____.
explanation: The governing rules are the Pakistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Rules, 1976. Do not confuse the 1973 Act with the rules.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 134, it is the duty of every Advocate to _____ and high standing of his profession, as well as his own dignity and high standing as a member thereof.
explanation: The rule imposes responsibility for the dignity and standing of both profession and individual advocate.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: According to Rule 135, a/an _____ shall not solicit professional employment by advertisement or any other means.
explanation: Advocates must not solicit. The rule allows limited ordinary cards, nameplates and directory listings that do not amount to personal advertising.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 137, an advocate shall not communicate about a _____ with a represented party in the absence and without consent of that party's advocate.
explanation: Subject of controversy is the statutory wording. Deal through represented parties' advocates or obtain the required consent.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: A client's _____ of additional advocates should not be regarded as want of confidence. Association as colleague should be declined unless the first advocate's dues are paid.
explanation: The rule uses proffer of assistance and leaves the decision to the client. It also protects unpaid dues of the first advocate.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 141, no division of fees with any person for legal services is _____ EXCEPT with another advocate based on division of work under their agreement.
explanation: Proper is the exact statutory word. The options are synonyms in ordinary speech, so this is a wording drill. The substantive exception is advocate-to-advocate division based on work.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 142, subject to precedence of the _____, advocates should maintain the order of precedence in the roll.
options: Vice Chairman and Pakistan Bar Council
explanation: The two offices are Attorney-General and Advocate-General, not the Bar Council.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 143, seniors are expected to be not only courteous but also _____ to junior members.
explanation: Helpful is the rule's word; juniors owe respect while seniors owe courtesy and help.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 144, where more than _____ advocate is engaged on a side, the senior has the right to lead and juniors assist.
explanation: More than one means two or more advocates. Leadership belongs to the senior unless the senior wants otherwise.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 145, an advocate _____ acquire an interest adverse to a client in the property or interest involved in the case.
explanation: Shall not imposes a prohibition. Client loyalty rules prevent acquiring this adverse interest.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 147, before accepting employment an advocate must disclose his _____, if any, with the adverse party and any interest in the subject matter.
explanation: Relation is the precise word; disclose both adverse-party relations and personal subject-matter interests before acceptance.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 148, an advocate shall not represent _____.
options: When he is relative of any party
explanation: The rule directly forbids representing conflicting interests.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 150, an advocate shall not commingle the client's property with _____ and must promptly report receipt of the client's money or property.
explanation: Keep client property separate from one's own and promptly report receipts. Both duties are in this rule.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 151, an advocate shall not advise commencement of prosecution or defence unless _____ in reference thereto, subject to the stated relationship exception.
explanation: The threshold word is consulted, not paid or formally hired. The rule contains an exception for an appropriate relation to party or subject matter.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 152, an advocate shall not advise the _____ of any law; this does not bar good-faith advice that a law is invalid.
explanation: Violation is prohibited. Good-faith legal advice challenging a law's validity is expressly excepted.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Rule 154 explains how the _____ of an advocate is to be determined.
explanation: Fees depend on listed considerations such as time, difficulty, skill and customary charges; no single factor controls.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 155, controversies with clients concerning _____ should be avoided so far as compatible with self-respect and reasonable recompense.
explanation: Compensation disputes should be avoided; suit should be used only to prevent injustice, imposition or fraud.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 156, it is _____ for an advocate to assert personal belief as an argument.
explanation: Personal belief in innocence or justice is not the proper argument; legal submissions should support the client's position.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 157, except when essential to the ends of justice, an advocate should _____ testifying in Court on behalf of his client.
explanation: Except for formal matters, a lawyer who is a witness should leave trial to other advocates. Avoid testifying unless essential to justice.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 160, an advocate shall not advise a person whose testimony establishes a _____ fact to avoid process, conceal himself or make testimony unavailable.
explanation: Material is the statutory term. Hiding such a witness undermines the administration of justice.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 163, the _____ of an advocate in public prosecution is not to convict, but to see justice done.
explanation: Justice is the primary duty. Suppressing facts or witnesses capable of showing innocence is reprehensible.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Non-observance or defiance of Pakistan Bar Council decisions/instructions is gross _____, defined in Rule 165.
explanation: The intended answer is B, but the cited rule is wrong. Rule 165 deals with judicial appointments; this duty appears in Rule 175-B. Exclude the uncorrected stem from scoring.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 166, advocates must appear when a matter is called and, if this is not possible, make _____.
explanation: Satisfactory alternative arrangements is the operative phrase. The book's sentence has a placement/wording error, cleaned here.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 167, an unengaged advocate should refrain from volunteering opinion or argument unless called upon in _____ by a judge or judicial officer.
explanation: The invitation must be in open court, and the opinion must be responsible and impartial.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 168, an advocate shall not accept a case out of spite or _____ or for delaying a matter.
options: For the purpose of harassing anyone
explanation: Harassment and deliberate delay are prohibited objectives of accepting employment or prosecuting an appeal.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 168, an advocate _____ accept employment to harass anyone or delay any matter.
explanation: Shall not is a prohibition. The book's garbled sentence is cleaned to express that rule.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 169, an advocate shall treat the witness of the adverse party with _____.
explanation: Fairness and due consideration extend to adverse witnesses and parties. Client hostility cannot excuse abuse.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: As per Rule 170, an advocate has the right to decline professional _____.
explanation: The intended word is employment, but the general right is Rule 171. Rule 170 requires declining cases intended merely to harass or injure. Exclude this wrong-rule stem from scoring.
cue: 170 must decline abuse; 171 may decline employment
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 173, an advocate shall not _____ nor appear before a public officer or body professionally without first disclosing the represented interests.
explanation: Disclosure must precede the professional communication or appearance before the public body.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 174, an advocate should not accept _____ in a matter on whose merits he previously acted judicially.
explanation: A former judicial role on the same merits prevents later acting as advocate on that matter.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 174-A, _____ his previous designation such as “Retired Justice”, “Ex Judge” or “Retired General” during practice as an advocate.
options: All advocates except the public prosecutor can use
explanation: The restriction applies to previous designations used as prefix, suffix or in other forms during practice; seniority does not exempt it.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 174-B, an advocate's nameplate or board shall not exceed _____.
explanation: The specified maximum is one and a half feet by two feet.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 175-A, breach of canons of professional _____ in Chapter XII is professional misconduct attracting discipline.
explanation: Conduct and etiquette is the chapter's phrase; violations may attract disciplinary action.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar

subject: Ethics
question: Under Rule 175-B, defiance of Pakistan Bar Council decisions or instructions is _____.
explanation: The rule expressly uses gross professional misconduct and covers the stated Bar bodies and advocates.
sourceTitle: Law GAT 600 Important MCQ’s — National Academy by Sir Umar
